title: Refresh Token Rotation Service
instructions: Implement `RefreshTokenService` in `refresh.py` (the exception classes are given). Tokens are opaque `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)` strings stored only as SHA-256 hex digests. `rotate` issues a new token in the same family, enforces the per-token TTL and the family maximum age, treats a replayed token as `GraceReuse` inside the grace window or `ReuseDetected` (revoking the family) after it, and `revoke_user` revokes all of a user's families. All state changes happen under one lock.

evidence.label: Rotation and login return fresh urlsafe tokens
Stores only SHA-256 digests, never plaintext tokens
Replaying a rotated token raises ReuseDetected and revokes the whole family
A replay inside the grace window raises GraceReuse and revokes nothing
With grace_s=0 any replay is ReuseDetected
Enforces the per-token TTL and the absolute family lifetime ("expired")
Rejects unknown tokens with "invalid"; reuse errors subclass InvalidRefreshToken
Reuse in one family does not revoke another family
revoke_user revokes every family of the user and returns the count
20 threads rotating the same token produce exactly one winner
